catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1/2 results Topline data 2027
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated results from a Phase 1b/2 monotherapy trial in previously treated advanced extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas showed a confirmed ORR of 40% and a median duration of response of 5.6 months with a manageable safety profile. The company also completed enrollment in the Phase 2 second-line expansion cohort of this study, supporting a potential accelerated pathway. These findings suggest meaningful activity in a population with limited options and inform upcoming registrational plans.
catalyst_text_evidence: In the Phase 1b/2 trial, zoci, a potential first-in-class DLL3-targeting antibody drug conjugate, demonstrated clinically meaningful responses in patients with previously treated advanced extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (epNECs), with a confirmed objective response rate (ORR) of 40.0% and a median duration of response (mDOR) of 5.6 months. Zoci demonstrated a manageable safety profile, with a treatment-related discontinuation rate of less than 1%, no treatment-related deaths, and a low rate of interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis (1.5%, 2 cases, both Grade 2). Zai Lab has completed enrollment in the Phase 2 second-line expansion cohort of the Phase 1b/2 zoci monotherapy trial. Zai will pursue a potential accelerated approval pathway for zoci in previously treated advanced epNECs based on results from Phase 1/2 trial, with topline data of the full epNEC population expected in 2027.

catalyst_text: Announced encouraging Phase 1b results in first-line ES-SCLC
detailed_catalyst_text: First clinical results from a global Phase 1b trial of the DLL3 antibody-drug conjugate combined with atezolizumab with and without carboplatin in first-line extensive-stage small cell lung cancer were reported. The doublet cohort showed an 81.8% confirmed objective response rate and 81.9% six-month progression-free survival with a favorable safety profile, while the triplet also showed high activity but with substantially more Grade ≥3 adverse events. These findings support continued development in this setting.
catalyst_text_evidence: Zai Lab Limited (NASDAQ:ZLAB, HKEX: 9688)), an innovation-driven, global biopharma company, today shared the first data from a global Phase 1b clinical trial evaluating zocilurtatug pelitecan (zoci, formerly ZL-1310) in combination with atezolizumab with and without carboplatin as first-line treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). Patients achieved a confirmed objective response rate (ORR) of 81.8% (95% CI: 64.5–93.0) by investigator assessment. The six-month progression-free survival (PFS) rate was 81.9%. Zoci plus atezolizumab therapy was well-tolerated; Grade >3 AEs related to zoci occurred in 9.1% (3/33) of patients treated at 1.6mg/kg. Patients in the trial who received the triplet regimen of zoci in combination with atezolizumab and carboplatin as first-line therapy (n=13) also demonstrated a high ORR (92.3%), with an mPFS of 8.4 months (95% CI: 3.7-NA) and mDOR of 7.7 months (2.6, NA) across all dose levels.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 3 topline results in myositis
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline data from the ALKIVIA Phase 3 trial in autoimmune myositis showed the primary endpoint was met in the combined IMNM and DM population. Patients on therapy achieved a 15.4-point greater mean TIS improvement at Week 52 versus placebo, with statistically significant benefit in IMNM. These results support a targeted FcRn approach in a setting with limited approved options.
catalyst_text_evidence: Zai Lab Limited (NASDAQ:ZLAB, HKEX: 9688)) and argenx ((Euronext &, NASDAQ:ARGX), today announced positive topline results from the ALKIVIA Phase 3 study evaluating VYVGART® Hytrulo (efgartigimod alfa and hyaluronidase-qvfc) in adults with autoimmune myositis. Study met its primary endpoint (p=0.0011) In the combined immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) and dermatomyositis (DM) population, patients treated with efgartigimod demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful 15.4 point greater improvement in mean Total Improvement Score (TIS) at Week 52 versus placebo (47.95 vs 32.56). In prespecified subtype analyses, the primary endpoint of Mean TIS at 52 weeks was also met in IMNM patients treated with efgartigimod (p=0.0048), with a 14.8 point greater improvement over placebo (45.05 vs 30.24).

catalyst_text_evidence: Zai Lab Limited (NASDAQ:ZLAB, HKEX: 9688)) today announced the European Medicines Agency (EMA) has granted Orphan Drug Designation (ODD) to zocilurtatug pelitecan (zoci, formerly ZL-1310), the Company's potential first-in-class Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), for the treatment of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (NECs). catalyst_text: Received NMPA approval for recurrent metastatic cervical cancer
detailed_catalyst_text: China’s NMPA approved the BLA for tisotumab vedotin to treat adults with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after progression on or after chemotherapy. The decision was supported by the Phase 3 innovaTV 301 trial demonstrating overall survival benefit, including in a China subpopulation. This marks the first ADC approved in China for this setting, expanding options for patients with limited therapies.
catalyst_text_evidence: Zai Lab Limited (NASDAQ:ZLAB, HKEX: 9688)) today announced that China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) has approved the Biologics License Application (BLA) for TIVDAK® (tisotumab vedotin for injection) for the treatment of adult patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with disease progression on or after chemotherapy. TIVDAK is the first antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) approved for the treatment of previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer in China. This approval is based on results from the global, randomized, Phase 3 innovaTV 301 clinical trial, which met its primary endpoint, demonstrating overall survival (OS) benefit in adult patients with previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer treated with TIVDAK compared to chemotherapy, including in an exploratory subpopulation of patients in China.

catalyst_text: Presented encouraging early phase data at AACR meeting
detailed_catalyst_text: Preliminary results from an ongoing registration-enabling multicenter Phase 1b/2 trial in epNEC and selected solid tumors were presented at a major oncology conference, showing an objective response rate of 38.2% in heavily pretreated patients with a manageable safety profile. These data support antitumor activity and tolerability, informing the path toward potential registration in epNEC.
catalyst_text_evidence: Zai Lab reported promising preliminary data from an ongoing registration-enabling multicenter, Phase 1b/2 clinical trial of zoci (NCT06885281) in patients with epNEC and other selected solid tumors at the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) Annual Meeting 2026 last month. In heavily pretreated patients enrolled in the Phase 1b/2 study, zoci demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity, including an objective response rate (ORR) of 38.2%. Zoci also demonstrated a manageable safety profile—neutrophil count decrease was the only grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse event occurring in more than one patient.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1/2 data presentation upcoming
detailed_catalyst_text: Announced preliminary results from a Phase 1b/2 study in extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas showing a 38.2% objective response rate across response-evaluable patients treated at 1.6 mg/kg. Patients were previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and other systemic therapies. Activity in this aggressive, previously treated population supports further development across DLL3-expressing NECs.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Additionally, researchers will share preliminary data from a Phase 1b/2 clinical trial of zoci (NCT06885281) in patients with extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (epNECs) and other selected solid tumors. These data indicate that zoci has antitumor activity, with an objective response rate (ORR) of 38.2% in an additional patient population with aggressive malignancies, poor prognosis, and limited treatment options.” “Preliminary results from the multicenter Phase 1b/2 study of zoci in patients with NECs demonstrated clinically meaningful responses.” “Researchers administered zoci intravenously at 1.6 mg/kg every three weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, with a data cutoff date of 2026-02-18, representing a median follow up of 3.7 months in the Phase 1b portion of the study.” “Among response evaluable patients, the overall response rate was 38.2% (13/34) across study cohorts and the overall disease control rate was 55.9% (19/34).”

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 1 intracranial data presentation upcoming
detailed_catalyst_text: Announced Phase 1 results showing strong intracranial efficacy in previously treated extensive-stage small cell lung cancer with baseline brain metastases, including a 53.7% confirmed iORR and 62.5% at 1.6 mg/kg. Safety was manageable with low rates of high-grade treatment-related adverse events. These results highlight meaningful CNS activity in a population with limited options.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Zai Lab Limited (NASDAQ:ZLAB, HKEX: 9688)) today announced clinical data indicating zocilurtatug pelitecan (zoci, formerly ZL-1310), a DLL3-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), provides rapid and robust intracranial responses in patients with previously treated extensive stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) and brain metastases…” “Results from an ongoing, global Phase 1 trial (NCT06179069) demonstrate that treatment with zoci results in significant intracranial lesion regression and reduced tumor size among patients with ES-SCLC whose cancer metastasized to the brain…” “In all patients with brain metastases and the opportunity to finish at least two post-baseline scans, intracranial objective response rate (iORR) among patients who received zoci was 53.7% (22/41), including seven complete responses. At the 1.6 mg/kg dose, confirmed iORR was 62.5% (10/16), including four complete responses.” “Zoci demonstrated a manageable safety profile, with most treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) reported as low grade with minimal discontinuation.”

catalyst_text: Dosed first participant in Phase 1 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: First participant was dosed in a global randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1/1b study in atopic dermatitis. The trial evaluates safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics in healthy volunteers and patients, marking the program’s entry into clinical testing.
catalyst_text_evidence: Zai Lab Limited (NASDAQ:ZLAB, HKEX: 9688)) today announced the dosing of the first participant in a global Phase 1/1b clinical trial evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of ZL-1503, a potential first-in-class IL-13/IL-31R bispecific antibody for the treatment of atopic dermatitis (AD). The Phase 1/1b study of ZL-1503 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled single-dose and multiple-ascending dose trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ZL-1503 in healthy volunteers and participants with moderate to severe AD.
